result.summary:
Read docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Verified: (1) cancelEvent's scope-boundary claim -- read apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts lines 651-676 directly: cancelEvent's body is exactly a status UPDATE + one audit_log INSERT inside one db.transaction, no registrations read/write anywhere, and its own header comment (lines 652-654) states the identical scope boundary the design cites verbatim ('no read of the registrations table, no notification composition/send of any kind. REQ-027's scope') -- the design's claim is accurate, not a misreading. (2) AC4's registrations-untouched property is structurally guaranteed: none of the three new functions (selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent, composeCancellationMessage, notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants) issue any UPDATE/DELETE against registrations -- confirmed by re-reading Sec2/Sec3 line by line; all three are read-only or write-only-to-notification_ledger via the existing sendLedgeredNotification. (3) The query in Sec2 excludes only admission='withdrawn' (WHERE eventId = ... AND admission <> 'withdrawn'), correctly including 'requested'/'waitlisted'/'admitted' -- matches AC1's '3 admitted, 2 waitlisted, 1 withdrawn = 5 notifications' arithmetic exactly; not an over-broad exclusion. (4) All 5 ACs map to a concrete design element in Sec7's table -- confirmed each row names a real function/field, no TBD language anywhere in the document. (5) All 3 named open questions (Sec8) are legitimate accepted/considered risks, not blockers: OQ1 (send-failure-after-ledger-commit) restates REQ-025 Sec3.2/REQ-026's already-accepted risk unchanged; OQ2 (narrow withdraw-vs-send race window) is residual risk of the same shape REQ-026 Sec9 already accepts, no AC exercises it; OQ3 (concurrent re-registration during the batch) is structurally blocked by registerForEvent's existing published-only guard, named only to confirm it was considered. None require rework.

FAILING CHECK -- zero-implementation-code (WF-02 Step 1b check 2d): Sec3's notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants rule, point 2, contains a fenced code block that is NOT a bare signature -- it is a full executable call expression with a concrete object literal and an inline arrow function: `sendLedgeredNotification({ db, sender, registrationId: candidate.registrationId, kind: "event_cancelled", classification: "transactional", userId: candidate.userId, composeMessage: (lang) => composeCancellationMessage(db, candidate.registrationId, eventTitle, lang) })`. This is structurally the exact violation class that FAILed REQ-026's design gate on its first pass (handoffs/WF02-REQ-026/step-01b-design-validator.json's original FAIL, reworked in commit 65704b4 per the regate handoff already on file: '.join() over an array literal, template-literal interpolation ... rather than this pipeline's required prose/table style'). An object-literal call with a lambda property is implementation, not a type/props specification -- per .claude/agents/code-designer.md's explicit rule, 'a function with a real ... statement in its body -- even a one-liner ... is implementation, full stop, regardless of how trivial the logic looks,' and this is a full call site, not even a function body. Must be rewritten as prose or a field/source table (as REQ-026's rework did for its own two flagged spots): e.g. a table of {field -> source} rows (db -> db; sender -> sender; registrationId -> candidate.registrationId; kind -> "event_cancelled"; classification -> "transactional"; userId -> candidate.userId; composeMessage -> a function of lang that calls composeCancellationMessage with (db, candidate.registrationId, eventTitle, lang)).

SECONDARY FINDING, same category, weaker but named for completeness: Sec5's handler-wiring paragraph quotes index.ts's existing and proposed lines as literal executable code (`bot.command("event_cancel", makeEventCancelHandler(db));` becoming `bot.command("event_cancel", makeEventCancelHandler(db, notificationSender));`) rather than describing the parameter addition in prose. Less severe than the Sec3 block (no computation, no lambda, just an added argument to an already-existing call), but should be restated as prose in the same rework pass for consistency with the rest of the document's discipline.

NON-BLOCKING JUDGMENT CALL (not a FAIL reason, recorded per this task's explicit instruction to state it): the synchronous-trigger-not-scheduled-job reasoning in Sec1 is sound as far as it goes (cancellation is a one-time command, not a time-threshold condition -- correct reason to reject the ScheduledJobDefinition mechanism), but the design never addresses a distinct risk that reasoning surfaces: apps/bot/src/index.ts line 195 calls bot.start() with no @grammyjs/runner concurrent dispatcher wired in, so grammy's default sequential long-polling processes one update at a time. notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants is awaited synchronously inside the /event_cancel handler, before the handler's own ctx.reply -- unlike REQ-026's reminder-job loops, which run in a background scheduled job and block no interactive command, this batch, for events with many non-withdrawn registrants, will delay the organizer's own confirmation AND hold up processing of every other user's bot interaction for the batch's duration (bounded by scheduler/rateLimiter.ts's 25-msg/sec pacing -- roughly 4s per 100 registrants, unbounded for larger N). No PRD volume/capacity figures for Release-1 chapter sizes were found in this repository to bound how large N can realistically get, so this cannot be dismissed as clearly out of range. It does not violate any AC or security invariant and no AC exercises event scale, so it is NOT added as a blocking FAIL reason here -- but CODE-DESIGNER should add it as a 4th named open question (accept the blocking risk explicitly at Release-1 scale, or choose fire-and-forget / a bounded concurrency approach) in the same rework pass, so it is not lost.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md Sec3, notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants rule point 2: fenced code block is an executable sendLedgeredNotification(...) call with a concrete object literal and an inline arrow function (composeMessage: (lang) => ...), not a bare signature -- forbidden implementation code per WF-02 Step 1b check 2d and .claude/agents/code-designer.md. Rewrite as prose/table (field -> source), matching REQ-026's rework precedent (commit 65704b4).

docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md Sec5, handler-wiring paragraph: index.ts's before/after wiring lines are quoted as literal executable call-expression code rather than described in prose. Restate as prose in the same rework pass.

docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md Sec8 (Open questions) does not name the synchronous-batch-blocks-the-bot's-single-threaded-long-poll-loop risk (apps/bot/src/index.ts:195 bot.start(), no concurrent runner) -- not a blocker (no AC exercises event scale, no repo-local PRD volume figures found to bound it), but should be added as a 4th named open question in the same rework pass rather than left unaddressed.
